about.title: Montague Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone is not a legal problem first. It is a loss. In a town of about 1,400 people like Montague, that loss tends to reach every street, from State Route 3 along 11th Street out to Ager Road and Big Springs Road. Public collision records for 2025 show one injury collision here, two people hurt and no traffic deaths, and a wrongful death claim is not limited to crashes anyway. It can follow a fatal fall on someone else's property, a medical error, a workplace accident, or a defective product. Under California law, a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children hold the first right to bring the claim; certain dependents and heirs may follow. The claim seeks funeral and burial costs, the financial support the person would have provided, and the harder-to-measure loss of love, companionship and guidance. It is a civil action, separate from any criminal charges. LawProactive connects Montague families with an independent attorney at no cost, and network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Montague Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who may file
items.desc: California limits who has standing to bring a wrongful death claim, starting with the spouse or domestic partner and children. An attorney in our network can sort out where your family stands before anything is filed.

items.title: The two-year deadline stays in view
items.desc: Most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and claims involving a government entity carry a much shorter window. Connecting early keeps those dates from slipping.

items.title: A civil claim that stands on its own
items.desc: Whether or not anyone is charged criminally, a wrongful death action is a separate civil matter seeking funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. The attorney you are matched with works on contingency.

items.question: Montague recorded no traffic deaths in 2025. Do wrongful death claims still come up in a town this small?
items.answer: Yes. Traffic crashes are only one source of these claims, and a single year's count says nothing about an individual family's circumstances. Deaths tied to medical care, workplaces, unsafe property or faulty products can all give rise to a claim in Siskiyou County. If your loss fits any of those patterns, it is worth a conversation with an attorney.

items.question: Who in my family is allowed to bring the claim?
items.answer: California gives first priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children of the person who died. If none exist, certain dependents and other heirs may have standing. Because these rules can get complicated in blended or extended families, an attorney can confirm who should be named before the case is filed.

items.question: What if a county road or state highway was involved in the death?
items.answer: When a public entity such as Siskiyou County or the State of California may share responsibility, a formal claim usually has to be presented far sooner than the general two-year deadline. Missing that shorter window can close off part of the case. Reaching out promptly gives the attorney time to identify every responsible party and meet each deadline.
